title: Entanglement Asymmetry in Random Quantum Automata
authors: Olalla A. Castro-Alvaredo, Dávid Szász-Schagrin, Michele Mazzoni
abstract: We investigate the subsystem entanglement asymmetry in random quantum automaton ensembles, which are generated by permuting the basis states in the Hilbert space and applying global phase shifts. We compute the ensemble average of the $U(1)$ subsystem asymmetry in different connectivity geometries, showing that the late-time limit of the ensemble associated to a 2-local circuit geometry coincides with the all-to-all ensemble average. By focusing on different subsystem sizes, we demonstrate that, similarly to Haar-random circuits, the system locally symmetrizes. However, in sharp contrast to the Haar-random setting, the scale at which symmetrization happens depends on the initial state, a phenomenon we associate with the interplay of conservation of the participation entropy and the uniform exploration of charge sectors. Additionally, we connect the growth of the subsystem asymmetry to the subsystem coherence and show that their growth is characterized by the same symmetrization scale.
summary: This paper analyzes subsystem entanglement asymmetry and coherence in systems evolving under Random Quantum Automata. It finds that the approach to equilibrium differs significantly from standard random unitary models because the dynamics conserve participation entropy. This leads to initial state dependence in the onset of local symmetrization, offering insights into how conservation laws shape quantum information spreading.
main_problem: The study investigates subsystem entanglement asymmetry in random quantum automaton ensembles (QAEs) compared to established models like Haar-random circuits.
main_result: Unlike Haar-random circuits, the scale at which local symmetrization occurs in QACs depends on the initial state due to the interplay between conserved participation entropy and charge sector exploration.
method: The authors compute ensemble averages of subsystem entanglement asymmetry using techniques involving replica vectorization formalism and asymptotic analysis for large system sizes.
model_or_system: The model involves Random Quantum Automata (QA gates), which operate by applying a random permutation of the computational basis followed by global phase shifts to a bipartite quantum system S=A U B.
key_observables: Subsystem entanglement asymmetry ($	ext{U}(1)$ symmetry related), participation entropy, and subsystem coherence are key observables analyzed across different subsystem sizes.
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the late-time limit, varying subsystem sizes ($L_A$), and comparing results to Haar-random circuit limits.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes self-averaging properties hold for ensemble averages and relies on approximations derived from the Choi-Jamiołkowski representation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically contrasts $	ext{R\'enyi-2}$ asymmetry and coherence in QAEs versus Haar states, showing initial state dependence. Figure 7 shows time evolution of average coherence for varying tilting angles under 2-local circuit dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the observables (asymmetry, purity) within the QAE framework, deriving formulas using advanced mathematical tools, establishing key relationships between different measures (e.g., coherence and purity), and finally analyzing the asymptotic behavior and time evolution in specific regimes.
why_interesting: It provides a detailed theoretical comparison of entanglement dynamics in structured random quantum circuits (QACs) versus unstructured ones (Haar), highlighting how underlying conservation laws modify expected thermalization/scrambling behaviors relevant to many-body physics.
